newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan orders banks to cuts lavish expenses.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan orders banks to cuts lavish expenses.

text.p: The State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) issued orders on Tuesday asking nationalised commercial banks (NCBs) and development finance institutions (DFIs) to cut lavish expenses and redefine their loan policies.

The orders, faxed to news organisations in the latest of a series issued to overhaul the NCBs and DFIs after it got greater autonomy early this month, also called for a ban on lavish expenses and excessive establishments and closure of rest houses maintained abroad.
A SBP order said the guest houses maintained by NCBs and DFIs must be closed and the properties and assets owned by the financial institutions must be auctioned.
The bank asked the NCBs and DFIs to redefine procedures for sanctioning, writing off and restructuring of stuck-up loans and loan recovery policies.
Bank loan default is one of the biggest problems, an SBP official said. "A vigorous campaign is being launched by the SBP to pursue wilful defaulters...so as to recover the due amount."
He said defaults of loans of one million rupees ($24,863) and above totalled more than 113 billion rupees ($2.80 billion) as on June 30 last.
